rechecks.stress: data/research/ws01/tmp/redteam_stress.py, redteam_stress2.py -> redteam_stress.json, redteam_stress2.json (closed trades, stationary bootstrap of entry days with blocks 5 / 20 / 60 d and max(5, p90 holding days); read-only on data/research/stress/trades)
rechecks.tvtp: data/research/ws01/tmp/redteam_tvtp.py -> redteam_tvtp.json (DM t of the M1h walk-forward log scores with HAC lags 8 (auto) / 24 / 72 / 168 h and day / week means)

findings.finding: zoo_ensemble 'SURVIVES' is knife-edge and does not survive a holding-period-matched bootstrap on closed trades. Closed trades: mean +0.317 R (n 2170); 95% CI with 5-day blocks [+0.003, +0.686] (re-run [+0.011, +0.683]), with 20-day blocks [-0.020, +0.701], with blocks = p90 holding period (32 d) [-0.004, +0.703], one-sided bootstrap P(mean <= 0) = 0.027. Median holding 6.8 d, p90 32 d, so the registered 5-day block is shorter than most trades.
findings.recommendation: Report zoo_ensemble as FRAGILE-positive (the strongest), not SURVIVES; set the stress bootstrap block to max(5, p90 holding days) per unit; stop citing 'zoo_ensemble SURVIVES' as evidence of edge for the trend_4h sleeve (agent/decision.py GATE_STRATEGY maps trend_4h to zoo_ensemble rules).

findings.finding: The holdout figure behind zoo_ensemble (+0.664 R on 151 trades) is driven by 20 positions still open at the data end and marked at the last close (+87.4 R, about +4.4 R each, the November sell-off). Closed holdout trades: +0.099 R on 131 trades, 95% CI [-0.73, +0.99] (P(<=0) 0.46), and -47.6 R in total without its 5 best trades. The holdout carries no information about the trend edge (MDE at 80% power about 1.1 R per trade; detecting +0.3 R needs about 1,700 closed holdout trades, about 5 years at the current rate).
findings.evidence: redteam_stress.json zoo_ensemble.hold_closed; stress report scorecard 'open at data end: 20, +87.4'
findings.recommendation: Make closed-trade statistics the primary verdict input, report open positions as censored (with their mark) in a sensitivity column; never let the data end date decide a holdout verdict.

findings.finding: Re-judged on closed trades with matched blocks (trade-level gates F1 / G5 / G6 / G7 recomputed, others as reported), no unit SURVIVES: geo_pivot_bo (closed holdout -0.155 R, CI with 55-day blocks [-0.000, +0.915]) and zoo_ensemble become FRAGILE; trend_4h stays FRAGILE (all-period CI [-0.035, +0.221]) although its closed holdout is the best (+0.43 R, n 266, CI [+0.02, +0.86] with 5-day blocks) and its in-sample is weak (+0.07 R, CI includes 0). FAILS units are unchanged.
findings.evidence: redteam_stress2.json (note: its G6 label also fires on CIs entirely below 0; that does not change any verdict because F1 fires first)
findings.recommendation: Replace the launch statement 'only the 4h trend family survives (zoo_ensemble SURVIVES)' with 'no unit passes every screen; zoo_ensemble and trend_4h are the strongest FRAGILE-positive units'.

findings.finding: Same zoo signals, two reads of the same clean holdout: H-TR1 (continuous ensemble positions, daily net P&L) recorded clean_holdout contradicts (portfolio Sharpe -0.42, NW t -0.32, 8 of 23 symbols positive); the stress trade layer (4-sigma exchange stop, |s| >= 0.3 entry, no re-entry after a stop) reads the holdout as positive. The second read under a different P&L definition after the first one failed is a forking path and was not counted as an extra trial of H-TR1.
findings.evidence: hypotheses_results.jsonl H-TR1 rows; stress report method 'Trade layer'
findings.recommendation: Register the trade-layer zoo_ensemble / trend_4h as their own hypothesis with forward-only confirmation (see H-WS01-9) and count the trial; keep R-PX-3 / R-PD-1 / R-PD-2 citing H-TR1 as contradicted in the holdout.

findings.finding: 23 units x 7 verdict gates without multiplicity control: SURVIVES is the maximum of 23 screens. Registry-wide, the zoo_ensemble row's CI-derived p (about 0.04) does not survive BH or BY at 10%; within the 23 units Holm would also reject it. The report itself states the verdicts are screens, not evidence of edge, but the program summary used them as evidence.
findings.recommendation: Quote stress verdicts as robustness screens only; any edge claim needs a family-wise or FDR-controlled test across the units screened.

findings.finding: Trend P&L is a tail: for zoo_ensemble the best 5% of closed trades make 191% of the total, i.e. the other 95% lose; the G7 gate (total without the 5 best trades) is applied to all trades, not to the holdout, where it fails (-47.6 R).
findings.recommendation: Apply G7 per segment; report the share of P&L from the top 5% of trades.

findings.finding: The only direction effect (first touch of the prior-day / prior-week high or low continues: +0.15-0.33 sigma vs placebo) is a tail, not a hit rate (continuation probability 0.46-0.49, same as placebo), 5-8 bp against about 15 bp of round-trip costs, and every executable rule built on it loses (H-GEO16, DSR 0 over 2,576 trials). The placebo levels sit 0.5-1.5 daily sigma away, so real and placebo touches differ in how far price travelled; only a post-hoc time-of-day match was checked, not a distance match.
findings.evidence: report sections 2 and Caveats ('Placebo design', 'A confound checked ... post-hoc')
findings.recommendation: Keep it as an expectation for risk (levels break more than hold, R-PX-4), not an entry signal; a distance-matched placebo is the registered follow-up if anyone wants to use it.

findings.finding: Cross-segment success rules recorded per segment: H-GEO1's rule needs rho_holdout >= 0.8 for variance and volume, but its llm_in_sample row is 'supports' while variance rho_holdout = 0.768; H-GEO6's rule needs the off-clock check in both DST regimes (fails in EST, 1.75) yet the holdout row is 'supports'. The hypothesis-level verdict is inconclusive in both cases.
findings.recommendation: Record a pooled, hypothesis-level verdict for cross-segment rules; the hour-of-week vol profile itself is robust elsewhere (H-NS4, H-GEO3).

findings.finding: Exemplary multiple-testing design: BH 10% over 156 cells in-sample, one-sided BH among the 15 survivors on the holdout (4 pass), DSR over 2,576 rule trials. Registry-wide, H-GEO9 survives BY10 in discovery (Bonferroni min-p 4e-10) but its holdout Simes p (0.15) makes the replication sign-only at the registry level.

'Informedness' is the 60 s markout side x (mid(t+60 s) - execution price) relative to the all-order mean. It includes each order's own permanent price impact and is not size-matched, while the types are defined by size, levels crossed and burst traits; the sweepers' +0.84 bp may be own impact of large multi-level orders rather than information. Registry-wide the result is robust statistically (t 13-22 over days), so the issue is interpretation, not significance.
findings.recommendation: Before using types to decide whom to quote against: markout from the post-trade mid (t + 1 s) to t + 60 s and a within-type regression on log(notional / L1); report permanent vs temporary impact.

findings.finding: HMM inputs (ln spread in bp, 5 bp bands) drift with the price level; house rule 1.3 (ADF + KPSS, PSI) was not run before the fit. Disclosed as a mistake; it inflated the H-PART4 60-min gain. Forward follow-up H-PART9 uses the type mix only, which is the right repair.
findings.recommendation: Apply the stationarity gate to every feature in the PART pipeline before H-PART9 is read.

findings.finding: Correct handling of overlap: the in-sample Wald p ~ 1e-23 on 250 k overlapping rows is explicitly discounted; verdicts rest on held-out R2 with CIs.

The holdout DM results are robust to the HAC choice. TVTP minus CTP (clean_holdout, 3,552 h, +0.0075 nats/row): t = 2.89 with the automatic lag (8 h), 3.01 / 3.02 / 2.80 with 24 / 72 / 168 h lags, 3.10 over 148 daily means and 2.94 over 22 weekly means. TVTP minus VAR: t 7.8-11.4, weekly 9.6. In-sample TVTP minus CTP stays insignificant (t 1.16-1.26).

The decision-relevant gain is calendar seasonality: most of the 0.31 nats/row over VARs is the weekend regime of 24/7 metals perps, and a seasonal VAR closes about three quarters of it (H-TVTP1s, post hoc and labelled). The in-sample segment is only 2026-03-09..07-01 (2,397 h), so every 'supports' rests on the holdout alone.
findings.recommendation: Use an hour-of-week scale factor (not the MS-VAR) for metals risk; it is the simpler spec that captures the gain.

findings.finding: The shared evaluate.newey_west_t uses lag = floor(4 (n/100)^(2/9)): 8 lags for 3,500 hourly rows, 10 for 13,000. Hourly loss or return series with daily / weekly seasonality or multi-day overlapping labels need far longer lags or block aggregation. It happened not to matter for TVTP (RT-TVTP-1), but every hourly study using it inherits the risk.
findings.recommendation: For hourly series report the day- or week-mean t alongside the automatic HAC t; for overlapping labels set the lag to at least the label horizon.

findings.finding: Holdout verdicts are sign-only by design (verdicts.py MIN_HOLDOUT = 8 and most study scripts), so a 'supports' row in clean_holdout is usually a sign agreement: 24 of 57 holdout supports with a statistic have p > 0.10, and registry-wide BY10 keeps 17 of 66 holdout supports.
findings.recommendation: Record the holdout statistic and n with every verdict, and grade rules on two-stage replication (discovery BY10, holdout BH10 among the selected), not on labels.
